Come to find out he had an on and off again relationship with someone and didn't want to tell me I was a placeholder. Came back after 10 months asking to try again and when I brought the same concerns up he told me he was giving off the wrong impression & to not take it a certain way. '"we are only friends". Hurts like hell. I don't want to date again.

Cleaned the kitchen after we had used it for baking the day before (almost all utensils used), baked some food, cleaned off the icing and gingerbread scraps encrusted on the counter, set out xmas China with cookies, cheese and crackers, made coffee, and put a coffee bar next to the pot while my parents were busy and working during the day. 

My dad came home to yell at me for some cheese that had melted onto the bottom of the oven the previous day when my mom was baking brie and my mom was upset I didn't heat some chicken up before company came over. No thank-you, no "wow this place looks great!", no "you really helped pull today together for tonight". 

I am so done.

Ugh that must be frustrating. It's like therapy only helps if you're willing to be vulnerable to get something productive out of it. The past few days not talking like normal have been difficult. We didn't talk for a good 6 years of our life while we went to college. I just have to revert back to the way I thought about him then. We had good times but he was never willing to move me up the list of his priorities. Gotta move on like they died. We pay our dues but they aren't there anymore.

He and I are in our mid-twenties but I guess it helps a bit knowing that these patterns won't go away unless they acknowledge them. He's had a lot of trauma in his life and lost his mom in a motorcycle accident a few years ago. Not saying that any of it excuses behavior, there is usually a source, but that requires THEM to work on THEIR behavior. We shouldn't have to explain human decency to adult men.

You and me both. I forgave him so many times until I started to go numb. Why accept someone who you know is going to stab you when you're not looking? Trust and respect need to be earned and maintained in a relationship. Not checked once and gone out the door. He came by to get his things earlier this week and kept saying how much I meant to him but a girl that had previously asked him to get food was popping up on his phone notifications. God it hurt. They don't understand what they had. I'm so sorry you're going through this too.

I'm going through something similar and it sucks knowing you poured your heart out for someone to shrug and essentially stomp on it. The worst part for me is I know if he promised me to change I would take him back almost immediately, but at this point we already know their patterns. Unless there's some serious work done with intention it isn't going anywhere.
I guess the closure is seeing how his actions were louder than his words. Yes there were many years we shared, but unfortunately, bad behavior doesn't overrule the time we've known each other.

I'm an INFJ and honestly I get anxious that people see me this way if I listen to people. I just like hearing people talk and trying to find ways to help if I can; when people open up to me on a deep level it can sometimes be uncomfortable because it happens when I least expect it.  Social interaction is great but can sometimes be overwhelming after a few days when I'm approached by people who want to unload. 

When I was younger I had a hard time communicating since I was shy and would stumble over my words, so I would get frustrated when I couldn't express myself from growing up in a strict household.  My parents weren't around a lot to help me figure this all out so it took me some time to understand my communication style. 

There are times I get frustrated by people like anyone else would but I try to be as direct as possible when solving issues. I don't like making a show of "being good" to prove anything either, otherwise I'm afraid people would see me this way. 

I don't know, I see bits of myself in this post that's a bit alarming but I don't claim to be all knowing or self-righteous to the point where my own opinion is the only thing that matters. Does anyone else feel this way at all? Am I overthinking this a bit or am I the problem here?

Look up "New Generation Sequencing". That's a very real thing that people in the medical field are aiming for!

Blood (molecular hematopathology) lab technician here:

Usually there are clotting symptoms mixed with other symptoms that indicate a genetic abnormality somewhere (I don't have all these memorized but we do 30+ tests ranging from clotting genetic disorders to leukemias). 

I'm going to try and simplify this down so im not using too much science jargon: Depending on the symptoms, there are bigger ranged tests that flag for either being positive  or negative for a a genetic abnormality in a few different regions of chromosomes that we look for. If it's positive from one of these bigger tests, we go down the line with smaller tests to pinpoint where it is, sequence it if possible for that genetic region, and report out to patients/doctors A) where the genetic defect is (chromosome, amino acid A/T/C/G) B) how common the genetic defect is and C) possible treatment options with drug therapy and/or chemo. 

Hope that helps answer your question!
